_comment: Named cluster shapes. Each one holds every answer the pg_deploy_cluster.sh wizard asks for, in the groups it asks them in. Deploy one with: ./pg_deploy_cluster.sh --topology 3-node. List them with --list-topologies.
_precedence: A flag on the command line beats the topology, which beats inventory defaults, which beats the built-in defaults. So --topology 3-node --pg-major 18 deploys the 3-node shape on PostgreSQL 18.

_groups._comment: A definition is written in these five groups, in this order, because they are the wizard's own questions. Every key is optional: omit one and the inventory default applies; omit a whole group and all of its defaults do.
_groups.hosts: 1) Which machines should the cluster run on?
_groups.install: 2) How should PostgreSQL and Spock be installed, and at which versions?
_groups.cluster: 3) How many Spock nodes, and what are they called?
_groups.components: 4) Which optional pgEdge components to install, and how each one arrives
_groups.availability: 5) Which nodes get a Patroni standby, and how it replicates

2-node.description: The smallest multi-master cluster: two Spock peers, each accepting writes and replicating to the other. No standby, so a lost node stays down until it is fixed while the other keeps serving.

3-node.description: Three Spock peers. Three hosts also make a fault-tolerant etcd: a two-host cluster loses its DCS with either machine, while three survive one. Still no standby — a failed node's data stays on that node until it returns.

2-node-ha.description: Two Spock peers, each with a Patroni standby that can be promoted if its node fails. Four PostgreSQL instances in all. Synchronous replication, so a committed write is on the standby before the client is told it committed.

2-node-extensions.description: The 2-node shape with every pgEdge component: lolor for replicated large objects, snowflake for collision-free int8 sequences, and the ACE consistency tool. lolor needs shared_preload_libraries, so the servers are restarted once during setup.

3-node-extensions.description: The 3-node shape with every pgEdge component, installed from the package repository. The shape to deploy when the cluster will be checked with --health_check spock,lolor,snowflake,ace: those suites need their components present.

3-node-extensions-source.description: Three Spock peers and all three components built from git rather than installed from packages. Everything compiles on every host, so expect 20-40 minutes per machine. Each component can name the branch or tag to build.

local-sandbox.description: Three Spock nodes on this machine alone, separated by port. No SSH, no other hardware, and no HA — every node shares one kernel and one disk. For trying the tool out, developing against a real mesh, or running the regression suites.

_field_notes._comment: Every key, under the group it belongs to. A key written in the wrong group is refused with the name of the right one, so the grouping is not merely decorative.

hosts._comment: A topology describes the shape, not the machines. Which hosts it lands on comes from configuration/inventory.json, so the same topology deploys to staging and to production without editing it. One Spock node per host; surplus nodes share hosts on ports base_port+1, +2, ...
hosts.host_source: inventory | localhost. 'inventory' uses the hosts already listed in the inventory file — the wizard's 'Use these hosts'. 'localhost' is the wizard's 'This machine only': it writes configuration/inventory.local.json and deploys there, leaving your real inventory untouched. The wizard's 'Enter host details now' has no equivalent here, because a topology is the answer to that question rather than another way of asking it.
hosts.inventory_file: Path to the inventory to deploy onto, if not configuration/inventory.json. A --inventory on the command line still wins.

install.deploy_mode: packages | source. A source build needs an exact pg_version and compiles on every host, 20-40 minutes each.
install.repo_channel: release | staging | daily. Which pgEdge repository packages come from — the server, Spock and any packaged component. Packages mode only; leave it empty for a source build.
install.pg_version: An exact version such as 17.11, or 19.0beta3. Required for a source build; for packages, empty means whatever the channel carries.
install.spock_branch: Source mode only: the git branch or tag to build. Empty means the default for the Spock major (v5_STABLE for spock50, main for spock60).

cluster.node_count: Spock nodes: multi-master peers, each leading a Patroni scope of its own and each holding different data.
cluster.cluster_name: Names the deployment: its state file, its Patroni scopes and its log directory.
cluster.base_port: First PostgreSQL port on each machine; instances sharing a machine take the next port up.
cluster.base_restapi_port: The same, for Patroni's REST API.
cluster.data_root: Where data directories and configuration are written on each host.
cluster.hba_cidrs: Extra networks to allow in pg_hba.conf, as a list of CIDRs. The cluster's own hosts are added automatically.

components._comment: One entry per optional pgEdge component, each saying how it arrives. install: packages | source | none. ref: for a source build, the branch or tag to build — omit it for the component's default branch, and leave it out entirely for a package, which comes at whatever version repo_channel carries. A packaged component uses the same channel as the server. Listing a component as 'none' is the same as leaving it out, but says so.
components.lolor: Large objects that replicate: stored in the lolor schema instead of the catalog, so Spock can carry them. Needs PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and must be in shared_preload_libraries — so selecting it costs one restart of every server during setup. Each Spock node gets a distinct lolor.node (1-15), which caps a lolor cluster at 15 Spock nodes; a standby inherits its leader's value.
components.snowflake: int8 sequences that embed a node id, so multi-master nodes cannot generate colliding keys. No preload and no restart. Each Spock node gets a distinct snowflake.node (1-1023); the default is deliberately invalid, so nextval() raises until it is set.
components.ace: The Active Consistency Engine: a Go command-line tool that compares nodes and repairs differences. Version-independent, so one pgedge-ace package serves every PostgreSQL and both families. It installs a binary on each host rather than an extension in a database, and there is nothing to CREATE. A source build compiles it with the Go version its go.mod requires, downloading that toolchain if the host's is older.
components.ordering: Components are installed on the hosts before the Spock mesh is cross-wired and created inside databases after it. zodan's spock.add_node checks that a joining node's database is clean, so creating an extension first would make the cluster impossible to wire together.
components.after_setup: A cluster deployed without a component can gain one later: ./pg_deploy_cluster.sh --add-component pgedge-lolor. The topology is the starting shape, not a limit.
components.pg_extensions: Alternative to the per-component entries: the packed --pg-extensions string, as name:mode[@ref] separated by commas. The two forms cannot be mixed in one topology.

availability.standby_of: Spock nodes that get a Patroni standby, as names: ["n1", "n2"]. A standby is a physical replica of that node alone, which Patroni can promote. It never holds a peer's data, so it protects a node against its own failure and nothing else.
availability.synchronous_mode: off | on | quorum, per scope. 'off' is asynchronous: a commit returns before the standby has it. Only meaningful where standby_of gives that scope a standby to wait for.
availability.synchronous_node_count: With synchronous_mode on or quorum, how many standbys must confirm a commit.
availability.synchronous_mode_strict: Block writes when no standby is available rather than silently falling back to asynchronous.
